## Verdict and scope

**Verdict: equivalent for the frozen modeled claim.** The published root is universally quantified over a real density \(\lambda\), assumes the inclusive threshold \(51/50\leq\lambda\), then a `FourArcCandidate λ` and its `SatisfiesCMVTypeIVHypotheses`, and concludes negation of `IsWeightedPerimeterMinimizer`. The record supplies \(0<h\leq1\) and \(0<\alpha<\pi/2\); the separate predicate supplies \(1<\lambda\) and \(\lambda\cos\alpha=h\). Its minimizer predicate ranges over every formal `AdmissibleCompetitor λ` with exactly equal weighted area. This is the frozen claim, including the endpoint \(h=1\), not a proof of the unqualified CMV isoperimetric conjecture.

The claim remains conditional on the formal coordinate model. `FinitePerimeterRegion` uses measurable carriers, integrability, and the density integral over the complete topological frontier. The source article's perimeter is formulated through finite-perimeter/reduced-boundary semantics. The manuscript correctly identifies that bridge, together with existence, regularity, symmetrization, and the global candidate classification, as remaining work.

## Evidence

The root partitions the density domain without a gap: the middle-face aggregate proves the closed interval \([51/50,33/32]\), compact cells prove \((33/32,9/7]\), and the cap-replacement theorem applies above \(9/7\), since its certified threshold \(1.2581840884\) is strictly below \(9/7\). Each seam is assigned to one branch. The scalar type-(iii) comparison is transferred through an actual admissible coordinate carrier with equal weighted area and strictly smaller canonical frontier perimeter; the high-density proof instead uses the geometric cap-replacement competitor.

The inventory has 850 non-generated declarations. This review contains one review for each, with inventory `code_sha256` copied into the required `source_sha256` field, and exactly two generated-family reviews. The corrected `cmv_type_four_not_minimizing` handoff now states the formal identity
\[
 P_{\rm rep}-P_{\rm candidate}=c\bigl(1-\lambda g(X)\bigr)<0,
\]
which agrees with `cap_replacement_perimeter_difference` and the strict inequality `P_rep < P_candidate`; the previous sign reversal is absent.

## Model and geometry fidelity

The formal strip density has value one on the closed interfaces \(|y|=1\) and value \(\lambda\) outside. The four-arc candidate realizes the prescribed positive curvature and principal exterior-angle branch, derives the source incidence relation, and proves its area and perimeter formulas. The type-(iii) realization includes branch-complete circular caps, an exposed lower segment, and a full-frontier calculation. The replacement realizes one upper cap of twice the area of either original exterior cap while retaining the core; its exposed lower chord is charged at density one.

## Certificate coverage

The compact family comprises the indexed exact-rational boxes joining boxes 2 through 1023, with the aggregate theorem covering \([33/32,9/7]\). The middle-face family comprises 113 indexed bricks, with the aggregate and two prototype cells covering \([51/50,33/32]\). These are kernel-checked interval certificates over slabs, not floating-point samples. Their family ledgers and representative declarations agree with the aggregate consumers used by the root.

## External-source check

The sole citation has a stable local locator: the frozen arXiv v1 manuscript, Section 3.2, Propositions 3.5, 3.6, and 3.9, Lemma 3.8, Conjecture 3.12, equations (26)--(27) on printed page 19, Theorem 3.16, and Remark 3.17. Those passages support the strip-density setting, type-(iii)/(iv) candidate context, source parameter formulas, the published partial exclusion, and the statement that type-(iv) remained unresolved below the present modeled cutoff. The manuscript does not attribute the new \(51/50\) certificate to the article.

## Disposition

Approve the author-supplied body content for the frozen modeled cutoff. The renderer-owned title, proof-credit block, repository locator, section scaffolding, and rendered Lean-reference HTML in the assembled manuscripts are outside the body-only format review. No unresolved mathematical, citation, main-body, or supplement-body critical error remains.
